Vs.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This rule by 3rd patty petitioners, directed against order No. 15 dated 15-6-2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Other Class Suit No. 80 of 2008 rejecting the application of the 3rd party petitioners under Rule 10 of Order 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure for adding them as defendants in the suit. 

 2. Plaintiff opposite party filed Other Class Suit No. 80 of 2008 for specific performance of a contract against principal defendant No. 1 and 2 in which petitioner before us filed application under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of civil Procedure for being added a party on the ground that Other Class Suit No. 61 of 2008 over the self same property has been tiled by applicant petitioner against the plaintiff defendant No.1 and 2 of this instant suit. It is further stated that petitioners have interest in the suit property as certain portion of land was gifted to them by original owner of the suit property and other Class suit No. 35 of 2009 filed by them is pending. It is also stated in the application that principal defendant, Mst. Khodeza Khatun by heba-bil-ewaj deed and also by sale deed, transferred 7.25 decimals of land to the applicant by different kabalas. Learned Judge on the ground that since the applicants are not party to the baina, they cannot be impleaded as a party in the suit. 

 3. Mr A J Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate, submits that, Other Suit No. 61 of 2008 and Other Suit No. 61 of 2008 and Other Suit No. 80 of 2008 are pending and the vendor of the opposite party, Khodeza Khatun divested her property to the applicant petitioner and lost her title over the suit property in favour of the applicant as such unless the applicant petitioners be impleaded as a party in the instant suit, no effective decree can be passed as possession is lying with the applicant petitioners. Learned Advocate further submits that the vendor of the opposite party is party to Other Suit No. 61 of 2008 and Other Suit No. 80 of 2008 and petitioner having in possession by dint of heba-bil-ewaj and also by oral gift from vendor of plaintiff opposite patty, as such the applicant petitioners are necessary party in the instant suit for passing effective decree as such the petitioners are necessary party not property party, to be impleaded to the suit. Learned Advocate lastly submits that by his time, during pendency of these suits. Khodeza Khatun died as such if the suit of the plaintiff opposite decreed, unless the applicant petitioner be impleaded in the instant suit, would be un executable as such, the petitioners under law, required to be impleaded in the suit. 

 4. Mr MA Azim Khair, with Mr Md Toufiq Inam, learned Advocates strongly opposed the sub- mission of the of the learned advocate for the petitioner on the ground that statement upon which petitioners wanted to be added as party if allowed will convert the suit form specific performance of a con- tract to a suit for declaration of title, which is not permissible in law as the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Golam Kader. Being dead his heirs Nurun Hahar Begum vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder; reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107 held that suit for specific performance of a contract cannot be converted to a suit for a declaration of title. Learned Advocate further submits that, in the instant suit, plaintiff opposite party prayed for decree to the effect that whether agreement or baina is genuine or not and that can be done only against his vendor, not against the petitioner who are not a party to the baina, as such, petitioners should not be added as party in the instant suit. 

 5. Petitioner in their application stated that they have acquired right, title and possession in the property settled by heba-bil-ewaj deed and filed earlier suit. It is seen from the statements that petitioners being son of the vendor of the plaintiff was inducted into possession by the father and petitioners are in possession as such, if decree be passed without their presence, the plaintiff opposite party in executing the decree 'shall' have to go for further litigation Mr MA Azim Khair, learned Advocate, submits that, principal defendant having been died, as such, petitioners, who are the heirs of defendant No. 1, can be added as substituted opposite party by filing application for substitution in the suit as such applicant should not be added as party as per provision of Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 8. Learned Advocate further submit that in implicating 3rd party petitioner inthe suit then their simple suit for specific performance of a contract would be changed to a suit for declaration which as per decision of Golam Kader being dead his heirs Nurun Nahar Begum vs Abdul Khaleque Coukider; 43 DLR (AD) 107, cannot be. In that decision it is held:- 

 "From the application for addition of party it appears that the present applicants are claiming by earlier alleged purchase a small fraction of the total land involved in the present suit. Their title Suit No.7 of 1969 involves a small fraction of the present suit land. The learned single Judge of the High Court Division found that appellant Nos. 1 and 2 have not made any specific averments to the effect that they are directly interested in any manner in the suit land. The present appellants are not claiming through the defendants of the present suit. They have set up an independent title of their own. Their averments in the application for addition of party disentitle them to be included within the framework of the present suit. That will convert the present suit for specific performance of contract into a suit for determination of title which is not permissible in law." 

 9. But in the instant suit the averments and statement made in the application under Order I Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure that 3rd party petitioner claimed the suit land on the basis of prior heba-bil-ewaj deed and also by purchase from defendant No. 1 and title and possession having been transferred and delivered to the applicant, as such, if any decree be passed against title and possession less defendant No. I then that decree would be unexecutable as it is a settled principle of law that no court could pass any decree which if passed would be unexecutable and in fractuous. As such this case is distinguishable from the decision cited by learned Advocate Mr Abdul Azim Khair, Here we may refer to the decision Ezahara Miah vs Shaher Banu, reported in 49 DLR (AD) 85 wherein the Appellate Division held that "The proper from of decree is to direct specific performance of contract between the vendor and the plaintiff and direct subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance so as to passon the title which resides in him to the plaintiff in order to avoid all controversies." 

 10. In this case it is seen that 3rd party petitioner on the basis of deed of gift and also purchase are possessing the suit land, as such, unless they-be made party in the instant suit, if there be any decree passed, that cannot be executed and no court can pass a decree which is unexecutable, Here we refer to the case of Nurul Islam vs Jamila Khatun, 53 DLR (AD) 45, where it is held that "In a suit for specific performance of contract for sale of immoveable property plaintiff is entitled to deliver of possession. A trespasser in the suit property is liable to be impleaded in the suit and evicted from the suit property to give effective relief to the plaintiff" 

 11. At present 3rd party petitioner has two legal arm for addition of party, one, implead by inheritance and another by way of added as party in the instant suit on independent count and both count petitioner can be added as necessary party. 

 14. The order dated 15-6-2009 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh in Other Class Suit No. 80 of2008 is set-aside. The application field under Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the 3rd party petitioner is allowed. Plaintiff opposite party-is directed to amend the plaint accordingly. The learned Judge is directed to proceed with suit in accordance with law.
